title: OpenHOI: Open-World Hand-Object Interaction Synthesis with Multimodal Large

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states OpenHOI 'achieves competitive performance compared to recent methods,' while the Introduction's contributions explicitly claim 'state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods by a large margin.' Section 4.3, however, states: 'Results in Tables 2 and 3 show marginal improvements in some metrics, though differences are within standard deviations reported by prior works... our approach has competitive performance but not a definitive advantage.' These three characterizations of the same results directly contradict one another.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 (Related Work comparison table) vs. Section 2 (Related Work) text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The comparison table marks HOIGPT [13] with a checkmark under '3D MLLM.' However, the Related Work text explicitly states: 'HOIGPT [13] and MotionGPT [16] adopt VQ-VAE tokenization and GPT-style architectures... these models operate primarily on discrete motion tokens and lack grounding in actual 3D perception or reasoning. They cannot perceive objects or environments in 3D nor reason about spatial affordances or constraints.' This directly contradicts the table's claim that HOIGPT possesses 3D MLLM capability.

Section 4.1 admits: 'the unseen testing set includes object instances and categories potentially overlapping with training, limiting strict unseen generalization claims. This split thus mainly evaluates in-distribution generation with partial domain shifts.' This directly undermines the repeated strong claims throughout the paper (abstract, introduction, contributions, conclusion) of 'promising generalization to novel categories,' 'generalizes robustly to unseen objects,' and 'strong compositional generalization across diverse scenarios.'

The ablation discussion first downplays the effect of removing components: 'Excluding physical refinement losses causes occasional penetrations and minor temporal incoherence, but many sequences remain physically valid. The improvement from these components is thus incremental.' Immediately after, the text contradicts this by stating: 'Without this guidance, the diffusion model exhibits two key failure modes: first, it fails to generate complete long-horizon HOI sequences... second, it produces physically unrealistic results with frequent object penetrations... Through direct optimization of these constraints... we achieve significant improvements.' These two passages describing the same ablation give opposite characterizations ('incremental'/'minor' vs. 'failure modes'/'significant improvements').

The text states 'where the weights λ_task, λ_aff are utilized to balance the different loss items,' implying a combined loss equation (e.g., L = λ_task·L_task + λ_aff·L_aff). However, no such equation is presented anywhere in the main text (no numbered equation defines this combination), leaving the 'where' clause referring to a non-existent formula.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, Implementation Details (Diffusion Model paragraph)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix A states: 'During sampling, we apply classifier-free guidance by randomly substituting 10% of conditioning inputs with unconditional noise while retaining 90% of the original conditions, and use a guidance scale of 2.5.' This contradicts Section 3.2, which correctly describes the 10% masking as occurring 'during training' ('we randomly mask 10% of the conditional inputs C during training to train the unconditional model'), not during sampling. Masking conditioning inputs is a training procedure for learning the unconditional model, not a sampling-time operation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B.3 (Sampling Process) vs. Tables A5/A6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix B.3 states 'where s ≥ 1 controls the guidance strength,' establishing a domain constraint for the classifier-free guidance scale. Yet the sensitivity analysis in Tables A5 and A6 ('Guidance Rate on GRAB/ARCTIC') tests a value of 0.5, violating the stated constraint s ≥ 1.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 5 (Ablation Study on ARCTIC), Seen 'w/o CFG' row
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Diversity value for 'w/o CFG' (Seen) is reported as 3.39 ± 0.18, which exactly matches the GT Diversity value (3.39) shown at the top of the same table. All other ablation rows (w/o Affordance: 2.03, w/o l_penetration: 2.45, w/o l_aff: 2.31, Ours: 2.65) deviate substantially from GT, making this exact match for 'w/o CFG' statistically implausible and suggestive of a copy-paste or transcription error.

The text states: 'we first perform coarse-grained fine-tuning on the Affordance dataset to instill strong affordance priors, and then carry out fine-grained tuning on the HOI dataset to produce our final model [43].' Reference [43] is 'SDEval: Safety Dynamic Evaluation for Multimodal Large Language Models,' a paper about safety evaluation of MLLMs, which has no relevance to the fine-tuning methodology being described. This is a mismatched/fabricated citation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table of Contents (C.9 'Statistically Insignificant') and Table A11 title vs. Section C.9 text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The table of contents lists the section as 'C.9 Statistically Insignificant' and Table A11 is titled 'Two-test Statistically Insignificant,' yet the actual section (titled 'C.9 Statistical Significance' in the body) states the opposite: 'the proposed method is significant at the 95% confidence level for the majority of metrics (p-value ≤ 0.05).' The majority of p-values reported in Table A11 are indeed below 0.05, supporting significance, directly contradicting the 'Insignificant' labeling in the table/contents.
